Pariah

puh-RY-uh · noun

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Pariah is an outcast; a person who is rejected or despised by a group or by society.

The whistleblower became a corporate pariah, informally banned from every conference in the industry.

Worked Example

After betraying the team's plans to a rival company, Daniel became such a pariah at work that colleagues stopped inviting him to lunch.

A pariah isn't just disliked -- they're actively excluded, shut out of the group they used to belong to.

How Pariah Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outcast

outcast: a person excluded from society or a group

untouchable: a person shunned or rejected by others

Antonyms

insider

insider: a person accepted as part of a group

darling

darling: a person especially loved or admired by a group

How Strong Is It? — outsider → pariah → leper

outsider vs. pariah

outsider vs. pariah: An outsider is simply someone not fully part of a group, without necessarily being actively rejected the way a pariah is.

leper vs. pariah

leper vs. pariah: Used figuratively, leper describes an extreme case of being shunned, as if the person were dangerous or diseased.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — paraiyar

root — paraiyar: a South Indian community historically assigned to low-status roles, including drumming, and treated as social outcasts under colonial-era caste systems (Tamil)

Put it together

Put it together: Pariah comes from the Tamil word paraiyar, the name of a South Indian community that colonial-era writers described (unfairly) as social outcasts; English borrowed the word and generalized it to mean any outcast.

Where it comes from

Where it comes from: Pariah is a borrowed name, not a built word: paraiyar is a real South Indian community that colonial-era writers unfairly branded as social outcasts. English took the community's name and stretched it to mean any outcast -- so the word's own history is a reminder that the label began as an injustice to real people.
